scope: Three confirmed malware archives and five individually assessed stranded members; all original SHA-256 values verified.
reverse_engineering: Read complete source, package entry points and metadata; inspected cleave facts including symbols, literals, value-flow limitations and decoded URL, and independently decoded every hex-table entry. No sample code or destructive commands were executed.

samples.marker_note: parser-session writer: concealed env/host export and response eval
samples.identification: parser-session 1.1.9 writer: concealed environment/host exporter and response-code loader
behavior: At module load, requires os and ../package.json, then builds one record from the entire process.env plus version, platform, hostname, username and noninternal IPv4-interface MAC addresses.

The hex-pair decoder maps slots to require, axios, post, an HTTPS endpoint, headers, a secret header/value and then. The exported arrow calls Axios POST with the collected record, evaluates response.data and discards promise rejection.
The POST happens on invocation of the exported function, not on import. The os queries occur while constructing module-level data.
samples.verdict_basis: Concealed bulk environment and host export plus eval of remote response has no logging/parser purpose. It is a malicious component even with broken archive wiring.
samples.missing_context: src/lib/writer.js resolves ../package.json to absent src/package.json. The supplied index imports an absent .pnpm/httpreslog path; the declared postinstall script is also absent. Runtime success and downstream returned code are unknown. No claim that specific credentials exist in the environment.
samples.hostile_coverage: Three hostile results: environment export, host/user identity export and remote response evaluation. These are distinct supported source/sink behaviors.

samples.marker_note: zlibxjson: fetches Discord EXE to AppData and launches silently
samples.identification: zlibxjson 8.2 main.py: Discord-hosted executable downloader and silent launcher
behavior: init reads APPDATA; if set, passes the fixed Discord executable URL and directory to download_file.
download_file creates the directory as needed, derives a basename from the URL without its query, streams requests.get response chunks into a wb file, and returns that same path.
init passes the returned path to run_silently, which calls subprocess.Popen(path, creationflags=subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW, shell=True). Errors during launch are printed.
The wheel console entry zlibxjson_command calls main:init. Ordinary package import only exports init; no install-time or automatic import-time download is inferred.
samples.verdict_basis: The package offers no JSON/compression behavior; its only substantive entry point silently downloads and executes a fixed third-party EXE in AppData, with placeholder package identity. This supports a malicious downloader verdict without asserting the EXE contents.
samples.missing_context: The final EXE, deployment authorization and runtime success are unknown. forager fetch of the exact URL returned HTTP 404; its filename alone does not identify a tool or malware family.
samples.hostile_coverage: Retained both suspicious linked-download/launch traits and added notable response-to-file and AppData-read observations. Investigated CDN source, AppData placement, hidden shell activation and verification absence: those also occur in legitimate updaters, so they do not justify a general hostile rule by themselves. No downstream theft/persistence/impact claim is supported; the hostile-intent gap remains.

samples.marker_note: osinthell p: empties regular files across drive roots
samples.identification: osinthell 1.6.9 p.js: drive-root file truncation action
behavior: Exported zero-argument function enumerates C, D, E and F drive roots, joins each entry to its root, tests statSync(...).isFile(), and writes an empty string with writeFileSync default flags.

The same file path flows from enumeration through the regular-file check into the destructive write. This is root-level truncation, not recursive traversal or secure erasure. Exceptions are swallowed at all loop levels.
samples.verdict_basis: Indiscriminately destroys ordinary file contents on fixed drive roots, without user selection, backup or utility output.
samples.missing_context: Which drives exist and which files are writable are unknown; execution requires a caller.
samples.hostile_coverage: Two existing hostile traits corroborate one destructive outcome. There are no additional independent attack outcomes in this 330-byte action, so adding a third hostile would duplicate or invent behavior.

samples.marker_note: osinthell v: silently force-deletes System32 DLLs recursively
samples.identification: osinthell 1.6.9 v.js: silent recursive System32 DLL destruction action
behavior: Destructures execSync from child_process and exports a zero-argument function whose only try-body command is del /F /S /Q C:\Windows\System32\*.dll.
Requests forced, recursive, quiet deletion of matching DLLs, discards stdio and swallows errors. It does not implement replacement, repair, backup or a target-selection interface.
samples.verdict_basis: A fixed-target, indiscriminate essential-DLL sweep wrapped solely to suppress its output and errors is a destructive payload. The broader deletion capability remains suspicious because servicing contexts are possible.
samples.missing_context: Privileges, protected/locked DLLs, the active Windows volume and runtime deletion success are unknown. No privilege escalation is inferred.
samples.hostile_coverage: Added one hostile result for the complete exported silent sweep; retained both suspicious general findings. This one action has no three distinct attack outcomes.

samples.marker_note: osinthell t: silently disables boot recovery and failure handling
behavior: Exports a zero-argument action issuing bcdedit /set {default} bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures, followed by bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No through execSync.

Each command requests shell parsing and discarded stdio; one empty catch swallows failure. Failure of the first command skips the second. No reboot, persistence, file encryption or elevation exists in this member.
samples.verdict_basis: A fixed boot-entry recovery-inhibition routine with suppressed output/errors and no repair/user-selection interface is likely malicious. The unrelated Utility package purpose and destructive call chain corroborate, rather than supply, the member byte evidence.
samples.missing_context: No deployment authorization, administrator rights or identity of the default loader entry is established. These operations can also be used by legitimate boot-management tools.
samples.hostile_coverage: Both operations are accurately suspicious. Investigated combining the pair, execSync, ignored stdio and empty catch: the combination cannot distinguish authorized boot management at hostile-rule precision. No unsupported hostile, ransomware or persistence rule was added. This remains a hostile-intent detection limitation, not a closed gap.

corrections_and_preservation: Four new YAML files add six findings. No shared rule was weakened, narrowed, relocated, suppressed or deleted. No old finding or severity was lost across the five members or all 55 archive analysis units (22 parser, 29 osinthell, 4 wheel).
controls: 20 assertions across 15 static source fixtures passed, including renamed bindings/endpoint, different POST body, different decoder radix, unrelated/unused host queries, different chunk/response/file bindings, targeted DLL servicing, visible stdio, logged exceptions and an unbound execution identifier. Existing 36 destructive assertions across 20 analyzed files and 5 boot-command controls passed. Both full hostile positives are registered in testdata/expectations.toml.
fetch_limits: Required forager fetch --all-wheels pkg:pypi/zlibxjson@8.2 attempted: PyPI JSON 404, browser fallback failed for missing ICU data. Original supplied wheel retained and hash-verified. Exact final EXE URL retrieval returned HTTP 404; no replacement sample was synthesized.
classifier_disagreements: Default live atomscan tiny output remains benign on p.js, t.js and main.py; v.js is suspicious. Writer becomes hostile. Archives remain convicted; parser classifier moves suspicious to hostile, others stay hostile. Atomscan warns model feature spec v18 is older than expected v21. No traits were duplicated or inflated to manipulate classification.
